From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:22:42 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unable to accept supplier invite — auth error (internal)

Ben / Jonas — pulled the logs for the NorthForge invite series. Short summary:

- The invite token is being minted with aud/issuer values derived from the tenant metadata. For tenants created after the November config rename we mistakenly left the legacy issuer key ("redwood-inference.dev") in the token generator instead of the production issuer ("redwood-api.redwoodai.com").
- When the acceptance page validates the JWT it checks issuer==expected_tenant_issuer and fails ("iss mismatch"). That's exactly what Sophie saw.
- Reproduced locally by creating a test tenant with the newer registry format.

I prepared a small patch to update the mapping used by the token-generator service; patch diff attached (patch-diff.txt). It’s a low-risk rename of the issuer lookup and a small unit test. If we roll to staging + quick smoke (5–10 min) we can push to prod with a config toggle.

Proposed plan:
1) Deploy patch to staging and run the acceptance flow for a NorthForge invite.
2) If green, deploy to prod in a short window and flip the config for tenants created after 2026-09-01.
3) Resend invite to Sophie / NorthForge and confirm acceptance.

ETA: staging -> prod in ~90 minutes if approved. No DB migrations.

Any objections or regulatory flags I should be aware of before we deploy?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Platform Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Hi Sophie — quick update and apology for the disruption.

Marissa pushed a targeted fix to the token-generator and we rolled the change to production at 15:40 PT. We then re-issued a fresh invite link for NorthForge (new token with correct issuer).

Can you please try the new invite link I just sent in a separate email? If you still see the error:
- Please try an incognito/private window (clears existing session cookies)
- If there’s an error, forward the page URL and the small numeric error code shown (if any) and we’ll take that as the trigger for a full session trace.

We’ve also scheduled a 15-minute follow-up call tomorrow at 10:00 PT to confirm vendor setup is complete and to review a short checklist so there are no other surprises. I’ll send a calendar invite shortly.

Root cause summary (brief): config key drift after a registry rename caused the token issuer lookup to return the legacy value for a subset of tenants. Fixed and added unit coverage + a short monitoring alert for any future iss mismatch spikes.

Apologies again — I know these invite hiccups are painful when a PO is waiting. We’ll waive the expedited onboarding fee for this onboarding as a courtesy (applied on our side).

Thanks for being patient,
